The audit spine: hash chain and evidence packs

After this lesson you can:
  • Explain the append-only, hash-chained audit record and tamper evidence
  • Describe what an evidence pack is and how exports stay governed
  • Connect audit lineage to decision replay

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. A chain, not a log
  2. Evidence packs: audit on demand
  3. Replay: the strongest form of proof
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. A chain, not a log

Ordinary logs can be edited; audit evidence must not be.

LoanOS seals every state change into a per-tenant, append-only SHA-256 hash chain: each event carries the hash of its predecessor, so deleting or altering any historical record breaks the chain visibly.

Verification re-walks the chain and reports integrity; external timestamp anchoring or WORM retention adds independent custody where configured.

Every event carries full provenance — actor, session, role, tenant, correlation lineage across API, UI, domain, decision and integration layers. This is the substrate for module 7's promise: 'who did what, on whose authority' is always answerable.

2. Evidence packs: audit on demand

When an auditor, inspector or court asks, the RE exports an evidence pack: a scoped, integrity-attested extract — authorised requester, purpose, date range and exact control scope recorded; only the scoped records and their integrity material included; tenant isolation and field-level restrictions preserved. Custody is part of the control: who generated, received and retained the pack, under legal-hold and deletion rules.

The operating mechanics live in the Guide's evidence-pack article; what a BA must grasp is the posture — evidence is *assembled from the chain*, never reconstructed from memory and screenshots.

3. Replay: the strongest form of proof

For decisions, the audit record does more than describe — it reproduces.

Because the decision engine is deterministic (module 3), the recorded inputs, policy version and model facts let anyone re-run a historical decision byte-identically.

'Why was this loan approved in March?'

is answered by replaying March, not by interviewing whoever was on shift.

That is the deepest sense in which compliance evidence is produced while the business flow runs.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-IT-GRC — Audit trails, integrity and assurance controls over IT processing.
  • RBI-IAM-SOD — Attribution and activity accountability, including WORM custody expectations.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. How does the audit chain make tampering visible?

  1. Access logs
  2. Each event embeds its predecessor's hash — altering history breaks every later link
  3. Daily backups
  4. Manager review
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Hash chaining means integrity is a mathematical property of the sequence, checkable by anyone re-walking it.

2. An auditor questions a two-year-old credit decision. The strongest available answer is…

  1. The underwriter's recollection
  2. The policy document from that year
  3. A byte-identical replay from the recorded inputs and policy version
  4. The approval email
Reveal answer and reasoning

C. Determinism plus recorded lineage lets the platform reproduce the decision exactly — evidence stronger than any narrative.
